probes.helperOutdatedTitle: The probe helper is older than this platform
probes.helperOutdatedBody: It will refuse requests it does not know yet. "Update helper" replaces it over the management channel; the probe checks the signature before it writes anything.
probes.helperUnsignedBody: This probe was enrolled before helper updates were signed, so it carries no key to check one against. Enroll it again - on the console with "probe enroll ADMIN@HOST --reenroll", or with a fresh invitation from "Add probe" - and the button below works from then on.
probes.noDeviations: The probe matches the desired state.
probes.planRestartWarning: This restarts the probe service. It reconnects afterwards.
probes.unenrollWarning: This removes the management access, the inventory and the NATS account of {{probe}}. The probe loses its connection; enrolling it again later hands it a new PRTG access key.

cleanup.uninstallMppHint: Removes the prtgmpprobe package, its configuration including the NATS CA, and the Paessler package source.
cleanup.sensorsSurviveHint: Without the probe software the sensors stay behind as services nothing calls.

enroll.title: Add probe
enroll.subtitle: The probe enrolls itself; you run one command on it.

step1.title: 1. What this probe becomes
step1.intro: Nothing reaches the probe yet. This only decides the name it will carry and the NATS account it will connect with.

step2.title: 2. Run this on the probe
step2.intro: Copy the command and run it on the host, as a user who can sudo. It fetches the CA, compares it against the fingerprint below, installs the restricted management access, and reports back.
step2.secretTitle: Treat the command as a secret
step2.secretBody: It carries a single-use invitation. Anyone who can read it can enroll a host under this account until it is used or expires.
step2.waitingHint: This page continues on its own as soon as the host reports in.
step2.deadTitle: This invitation can no longer be used
step2.deadBody: It expired or was revoked, and the command above would be refused. Create a new invitation to enroll this probe.

install_wireguard.title: Provide WireGuard
install_wireguard.note: Debian and Ubuntu carry the package in the main archive. On RHEL 9 it comes from EPEL, which has to be enabled first.

build_tunnel.title: Build the tunnel to the platform
build_tunnel.note: The probe reaches the platform afterwards. Check with “sudo wg show” – there has to be a time under “latest handshake”.

enroll.title: Start the enrollment
enroll.note: Fetches the CA first and compares it against the fingerprint below, then installs. This takes a few minutes.

step2.stepSecret: This command carries the probe’s private WireGuard key. Hand it over the way you would hand over a password – not by ticket, chat or email.

step3.title: 3. The platform takes over
step3.intro: The host reported in. From here the platform pins its host key, creates the account, writes the inventory and configures the probe.
step3.doneBody: It connects to NATS on its own from now on. Sensors can be deployed to it like any other probe.
step3.donePrtg: Two steps are still missing in PRTG: add the access key to the core's access-key list, then approve the probe. The key is on the probe's page under "PRTG access key".
step3.failedBody: The log below says where it stopped. If the cause was temporary, retry the job; if the host has to run the command again, create a new invitation.

fields.accountHint: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. Also becomes the name of the NATS account the probe gets automatically.
fields.probeNameHint: What PRTG shows. Derived from the host name if left empty. No spaces.
fields.hostHint: How the platform reaches the probe afterwards. Left empty, the address the host reports from is used - which is wrong if it sits behind NAT.
fields.installPackageHint: Leave this on unless the package is already installed and managed elsewhere.
fields.overlayBootstrap: This probe cannot reach the platform directly
fields.overlayBootstrapHint: For a site with no site-to-site VPN. The script then builds the WireGuard tunnel first and reports in over it.
fields.overlayBootstrapWarning: The script carries the probe's private WireGuard key in this case. It does not belong in a ticket, a chat or an email - hand it over the way you would hand over a password.
fields.ttlHint: How long the command can be run on the probe. For a colleague on site it may be longer.

interfaces.defaultRouteHint: This interface carries the default route. Reserving it would cut the host’s connection; the probe refuses it.

infrastructure.containersEmpty: No container of the stack is running.
infrastructure.iperfSubtitle: The measurement endpoints the iperf-throughput sensor measures against
infrastructure.iperfEmpty: No measurement endpoint is set up.
infrastructure.keyMismatch: The certificate and its private key do not belong together.

iperf.addIntro: The host is checked first, then the platform signs in once over SSH and sets the endpoint up itself. It keeps only a narrow access of its own; the credentials from here are not stored.
iperf.adminHint: An account that may become root on that host. Used for this one connection.
iperf.credentialBody: They are good for one connection, are not stored, not logged and not written into the job. Afterwards the platform holds its own restricted key.
iperf.credentialTitle: These credentials do not stay here
iperf.foreignUserHint: Leave empty for an endpoint that measures unauthenticated.
iperf.hostHint: The address the probes measure against, and the one this platform reaches over SSH.
iperf.keepServiceHint: Only takes the credentials off the probes and forgets the record. The iperf3 service stays as it is.
iperf.keysKnown: This host is already pinned to exactly these keys.
iperf.keysNew: This host is not known yet. Compare the fingerprint before any credential goes there.
iperf.nameHint: The probes carry the credentials under this name, and the sensor names it later.
iperf.nameShape: Letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen.
iperf.privateKeyHint: Instead of a password. Not stored.
iperf.publicKeyHint: The endpoint's public.pem, pasted whole with its BEGIN and END lines. Without it the probes cannot authenticate; an OpenSSH key (ssh-rsa AAAAB3…) is a different format and does not work.
iperf.registerIntro: For a host somebody else operates: nothing is installed and nothing is reached. Only the record here, so the probes can use it.
iperf.setupHelp: How the operator sets this endpoint up
iperf.setupHelpIntro: This host is not touched from here. Whoever is root there runs the following once - or setup-iperf3-endpoint.sh from the repository, which does the same and checks itself.
iperf.setupHelpService: iperf3 stores no password, only the SHA-256 of "{user}password", and decrypts what the probes send with the private key. The drop-in replaces the packaged ExecStart - without it the endpoint answers everyone.
iperf.setupHelpCheck: Then the counter-check, on the endpoint itself: the first command has to fail and the second one has to succeed. An endpoint that still answers without credentials looks exactly like a working one.
iperf.setupHelpBackTitle: What has to come back from there
iperf.setupHelpBackBody: The user name, the password the last two lines print, and the contents of /etc/iperf3/public.pem - the three fields below. The password cannot be read back from that host afterwards, because only its hash is on disk.
iperf.removeBody: "{{name}}" is taken off {{count}} probe(s), removed from its host and forgotten here.
iperf.removeForeign: Somebody else operates this host. Only the record here and the credentials on the probes are removed.
iperf.removePackage: The iperf3 package is not uninstalled - something else on that host may be using it.
iperf.updateForeignBody: The operator has already changed the password for "{{name}}". This stores the replacement here and deploys it to {{count}} probe(s). The endpoint is not contacted.
iperf.updateForeignHint: The password is stored only in protected runtime and in the profiles on current holders. It is not written to the job or audit log.
iperf.sourceCidrHint: The network the host will accept this platform from. Leave empty when IPERF_SSH_SOURCE_CIDR is set. Several, separated by commas.
iperf.startedBody: The platform signs in, installs the access and sets up iperf3. The job carries the progress.
iperf.startedTitle: The endpoint is being set up
iperf.rotateBody: A new password is set for "{{name}}" and handed to the {{count}} probe(s) measuring against it.
iperf.probesBody: Pick the probes that should hold the credentials of {{name}}. A probe taken out here stays out: deploying the sensor reads the same assignment.
iperf.notDeployedTitle: No probe holds this endpoint yet
iperf.notDeployedBody: The record exists, but no probe knows the credentials. Until one does, no sensor can measure against this endpoint.
iperf.prtgTitle: Which probes, and what goes into PRTG
iperf.prtgIntro: What a sensor object in PRTG needs as parameters depends on the probe: if it holds only this one endpoint, the sensor reads address, port and user by itself.
iperf.defaultAliasHint: This probe holds only this endpoint and therefore carries the "default" profile. The sensor object needs no connection parameter.
iperf.manualHint: Without a deployed endpoint, --server, --username and --password have to be written into the sensor object by hand.
iperf.aliasLostTitle: Existing sensors on these probes stop measuring
iperf.aliasLostBody: These probes hold exactly one endpoint and therefore carry the "default" profile: {{probes}}. With the second it goes away: objects without --server turn red, objects naming one keep measuring without a sign-in, unnoticed. Add --profile <name> to each affected PRTG object first.
iperf.aliasReturnsBody: These probes will hold only one endpoint afterwards and get the "default" profile back: {{probes}}. A --profile already entered stays correct, but is no longer needed.
iperf.sensorMissingTitle: The credentials are there, but nothing reads them
iperf.sensorMissingBody: These probes hold the endpoint but do not have "{{sensor}}" installed: {{probes}}. Until the sensor is deployed, nothing is measured.
iperf.startedNext: After that the endpoint appears in the list. From there it is assigned to probes and the sensor is deployed - only then is anything measured.
iperf.addStep1: 1. Name the host and read its keys
iperf.addStep2: 2. Sign in once and set it up
iperf.addStep2Preview: After this, the dialog asks for an account that may become root on the host - with a password or a private key. It is good for this one connection.
iperf.inviteTitle: Set up an endpoint by invitation
iperf.inviteIntro: For a host this platform cannot reach over SSH - behind NAT or a firewall. It gets a command, sets itself up and reports back; the only thing it has to reach is this platform.
iperf.inviteHostHint: The address the probes measure against. Leave empty if the host brings it along when it reports back.
iperf.inviteTtlHint: How long the command can be run on the host.
iperf.inviteCommandIntro: Run this command on the endpoint host, as a user with sudo. It sets up iperf3, installs the access for this platform and reports back.
iperf.inviteSecretBody: The command carries a single-use invitation. Whoever can read it can enroll a host as this endpoint until it is spent or expires.
iperf.inviteDeadTitle: This invitation can no longer be used
iperf.inviteDeadBody: It expired or was revoked; the command would be refused.
iperf.inviteProgress: The host reported in. The platform installs the access and writes the record.

overlay.title: Overlay
overlay.subtitle: The WireGuard tunnel between this host and the probes
overlay.modeLegend: When NATS traffic takes the tunnel
overlay.offWarning: Switching a probe off goes over its ordinary address. A probe that does not answer there is refused rather than left unreachable.
overlay.removeBody: Take {{count}} probe(s) off the overlay. They keep reaching this installation the ordinary way.

off.name: Off
off.hint: No tunnel. The probe reaches NATS the ordinary way.

auto.name: Auto
auto.hint: Tunnel up. NATS takes it only while the direct path is down.

on.name: On
on.hint: Tunnel up. NATS always takes it.

disabled.title: The overlay is off for this installation
disabled.body: Nothing runs for it until an administrator turns it on. Probes are unaffected either way.

hubDown.title: The hub interface is not up
hubDown.body: The overlay is enabled but the interface does not exist. Check the prtg-nats-overlay container; without it no probe can reach this host through the tunnel.

empty.title: No probe is on the overlay
empty.hint: Add one below. It keeps its ordinary address either way.

add.title: Add probes
add.body: {{count}} enrolled probe(s) are not on the overlay yet.
add.dialog: The probe generates its own key and reports back the public half. Its ordinary address stays as it is.
add.allOn: Every probe is on the overlay

enable.title: Turn the overlay on
enable.body: This starts the hub on this host and generates its key. Probes stay where they are until you add them.
enable.endpointHint: The address probes dial. It has to be reachable when the ordinary path is not, so on a site whose NATS address is internal, this is the public one. It cannot be the NATS address itself.

disable.title: Turn the overlay off
disable.body: The hub stops; every probe keeps its address and key and stays reachable the ordinary way. Put probes in mode "On" back to "Auto" first - their tunnel is gone afterwards.

errors.title: Something went wrong

common.validation_failed: The values submitted were not accepted.
common.conflict: This conflicts with the current state.

auth.invalid_credentials: User name or password is wrong.
auth.account_locked: Too many failed attempts. Try again in {{retry_after_seconds}} seconds.
auth.setup_required: No account exists yet. Create the first administrator.

probe.unreachable: The probe "{{probe}}" did not answer over the management channel.
probe.unreachable.cause: The host is down, the network path is blocked, or the management key was removed on the probe.
probe.unreachable.action: Check that the host is reachable and that the SSH service accepts the management key, then run the job again.
probe.protocol_error: The probe answered in a way the management protocol does not allow.
probe.protocol_error.cause: The probe helper on the target is older or newer than this platform expects.
probe.protocol_error.action: Update the probe helper on the target system.
probe.request_rejected.cause: The probe validated the request and declined it. The technical details carry its own message.
probe.request_rejected.action: Read the technical details, correct the cause, then run the job again.
probe.helper_outdated: The probe does not know the request "{{command}}" yet.
probe.helper_outdated.cause: Its management helper is older than this platform. Nothing about the request was wrong - the probe simply predates it.
probe.helper_outdated.action: Renew the helper on the probe page with "Update helper", then run the job again. A probe that was enrolled before signed updates has to be enrolled again first; its page says so.
probe.package_missing: No prtgmpprobe package is installed on "{{probe}}".
probe.package_missing.cause: The package only reaches a probe with the bootstrap command. It was removed by an unenrollment with "Uninstall probe software", or its installation failed - the technical details then carry that message.
probe.package_missing.action: Create a fresh invitation and run the command on the probe. The bootstrap skips a package that is already there.
probe.host_key_mismatch: The host "{{host}}" presented a different SSH host key than the one on record.
probe.host_key_mismatch.cause: Either the host was rebuilt and has new keys, or something else is answering at that address. Pinned: {{pinned}}. Offered: {{offered}}.
probe.host_key_mismatch.action: Confirm out of band whether the host was rebuilt. If it was, remove the old entry deliberately and enroll again; if it was not, stop and investigate.
probe.host_already_enrolled: The address "{{host}}" is already enrolled as "{{probe}}".
probe.host_already_enrolled.cause: The management access lives on the host, not in an inventory entry. A second entry for the same address would share it, and retiring either one would revoke it for both - leaving a probe that is connected to NATS and unreachable at the same time.
probe.host_already_enrolled.action: Enroll this host again under "{{probe}}" if that is what you meant. To give it a different account, remove "{{probe}}" first - that also revokes the management access on the host, which the next enrollment installs again.

nats.reload_refused.cause: Some settings cannot be applied without a restart - a changed server name above all. The change is written to disk and is not active yet.
nats.reload_refused.action: Restart the NATS server from the maintenance page (Infrastructure → Maintenance). Every probe and the PRTG core reconnect afterwards.

docker.unavailable: Container control is not available in this installation.
docker.unavailable.cause: The Docker socket is not mounted into the backend container.
docker.unavailable.action: Mount /var/run/docker.sock, or perform this action on the server.

runtime.incomplete: The installation state under runtime/ is missing or incomplete.
runtime.incomplete.cause: The stack has not been set up in this directory, or the backend cannot read it.
runtime.incomplete.action: Run the stack setup on the server and check that runtime/ is mounted readable.

jobs.unknown_type: This job type is not known to the platform.
jobs.orphaned: The worker did not report back. The job was ended and its locks were released.
jobs.all_targets_failed: The job failed on every target.
jobs.all_targets_failed.cause: Each target reported its own reason; the log lists them per target.
jobs.all_targets_failed.action: Read the log, fix what it reports, then run the job again.
jobs.some_targets_failed: The job failed on {{failed}} of its targets.
jobs.some_targets_failed.cause: The remaining targets succeeded. Only the failed ones need attention.
jobs.some_targets_failed.action: Read the log for the failed targets, then run the job again.

network.unreachable: The management API cannot be reached.

enrollment.token_invalid: This enrollment invitation cannot be used.
enrollment.token_invalid.cause: It is unknown, expired, already used, or was revoked. An invitation is good for one host, once.
enrollment.token_invalid.action: Create a new invitation and run the command it gives you on the host.

errors.stack.update_blocked: The update cannot start right now ({{reason}})

alerts.certificate.mismatched: The {{certificate}} certificate does not match its key

credentials.title: NATS accounts
credentials.subtitle: The credentials probes and the PRTG core sign in with
credentials.createHint: The password is generated and stored in the protected credential file. Reveal it only when the PRTG core needs it typed in.
credentials.rotateWarning: A new password is generated for {{account}}. The current one stops working immediately.
credentials.rotateProbeHint: The enrolled probe receives the new password in the same job and reconnects with it.
credentials.deleteBlockedProbe: A probe is enrolled for this account.
credentials.deleteWarning: The account {{account}} and its credentials are removed from the server. A client still using them loses its connection on the next reconnect.
credentials.revealHint: This disclosure has been recorded in the audit trail. Paste the value where it is needed and close this dialog.
credentials.autoHint: Accounts of enrolled probes come and go with the probe. This page manages what goes beyond that - the PRTG core account, for instance.

updates.title: Updates
updates.running_unknown: unknown - built without a version stamp; the next ./prtg-nats update fills it in
updates.unreachable: The repository could not be reached
updates.what_happens: The runtime is archived first, then the images are built, then the stack is recreated. The interface is unavailable for a few minutes while that happens.

rebuild_pending.title: The checkout is ahead of what is running
rebuild_pending.body: Somebody has pulled on this host without rebuilding, so the stack still runs the older code. Rebuilding installs what the checkout already holds; nothing is fetched and the checkout is not moved.

dirty_blocks.title: The checkout has uncommitted changes
dirty_blocks.body: An update would have to move over them. Commit or discard them on the host first - nothing here will throw local work away.

away.title: The stack is being replaced
away.body: The interface comes back on its own once the new containers are up. This takes a few minutes; leaving the page is safe.
away.stuck_title: The service has not come back
away.stuck: Something went wrong during the restart. On the host, docker compose logs web-api says what, and the runtime archive taken before the update is in runtime/archive/.

unavailable.title: This installation cannot update itself
unavailable.docker_socket_missing: The Docker socket is not mounted, so nothing here can build or restart containers.
unavailable.checkout_not_found: The stack was not started with Compose, so the checkout it was built from cannot be located.
unavailable.updater_image_missing: The updater image does not exist yet. Run ./prtg-nats update on the host once; every update after that works from here.
unavailable.unknown: The reason could not be determined.

system.title: Maintenance
system.subtitle: Verify, back up, restart - the hands-on work on the server itself.

verify.title: Verify the installation
verify.body: Runs the same check as ./prtg-nats verify: containers, certificates, runtime directory, NATS reachability. The result is in the job.

restart.title: Restart NATS
restart.body: Restarts the NATS container. Every probe and the PRTG core reconnect afterwards.
restart.confirmBody: All probes and the core briefly lose their connection and reconnect. Measurements of that moment are lost.

backup.title: Backups
backup.body: The JetStream backup holds the message store; the runtime export archives the whole runtime directory for migration or recovery.
backup.exportWarning: The archive contains the CA key, every account and every password in the clear. It belongs in a safe place, not in a ticket.

backups.title: Existing archives
backups.empty: No archive sits in the runtime directory yet.
backups.hint: The archives live in the runtime volume under backups/. Retention and rotation stay with operations.
